status_summary: The FY2026 request listed 24 Air Force F-35A, half the 48 previously projected, and the FY2026 defense appropriations approved by Congress on 2026-02-03 added 402 million dollars for F-35A procurement, 500 million for the F-47 and 474 million for two EA-37B Compass Call aircraft; the White House says the President signed H.R. 7148, the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, the same day. Exchange Monitor reported on 2026-02-24 that the 2025 reconciliation funding includes 4.5 billion dollars to accelerate B-21 production. The FY2027 request seeks 38 F-35A and about 338.8 billion dollars for the Air Force and Space Force, reported as more than 90 billion above FY2026 enacted levels. No action on pass-through funding, a B-21 rate of 15 to 18 a year, or an EC-37B fleet of 20 was found.

title: Air Force: end pass-through budgeting, grow 5 percent real, buy more F-35A, B-21, EC-37B
uncertainties: The Senate committee release gives the F-35A line as a dollar increase, not an aircraft count, so the number of F-35A funded in FY2026 was not confirmed (TWZ says 47 F-35 of all types were funded). The White House notice does not list the contents of H.R. 7148; that it carries the defense act is an inference from the same-day congressional approval and a House committee release counting 11 of 12 FY2026 bills done. The 4.5 billion dollar B-21 figure comes from Exchange Monitor citing the contractor and was not traced to a section of P.L. 119-21. TWZ notes the FY2027 budget documents appear to show a year-over-year cut of more than 4.2 billion dollars to B-21 procurement. Pass-through funding was not mentioned in the sources and no 5 percent real growth calculation was done: the roughly 90 billion increase is a nominal figure including proposed mandatory funds, and the FY2027 request is not enacted. The EC-37B fleet count could not be compared.
